t: Estimates of the Ottoman army run from about 45,000 to 100,000, while the Hungarians numbered some 25,000 to 30,000; the figures differ from passage to passage and between historians.

The Hungarian charge drove back the Ottoman front line, but Ibrahim Pasha's centre fell back in a crescent and the Hungarians, caught in the open between wings, cannon and Janissary fire, were encircled.
King Louis II and more than 1,000 nobles died, and about 2,000 captured Hungarians were executed afterwards; the kingdom was later split in three, and Hungarians still say 'More was lost at Mohács'.
dyk: King Louis II drowned in the marshy ground by the Csele stream, weighed down by his armour, and his body was found weeks later buried in the mud.
ev: A peasant rebellion led by György Dózsa is crushed by the nobles under John Zápolya
The Ottomans take Nándorfehérvár (Belgrade) and Szabács, leaving most of southern Hungary indefensible
Suleiman leaves Constantinople at the head of the Ottoman army and advances up the Danube
The Ottoman army defeats the Hungarians near Mohács and King Louis II dies
Buda is occupied and burned, and the Ottoman army withdraws to Constantinople
The Ottomans decide to occupy Buda after the siege of that year
The battlefield becomes a national historical memorial site on the 450th anniversary

f.place: A wide, waterlogged plain near the village of Mohács in the Kingdom of Hungary, on the Danube
f.sides: The Kingdom of Hungary under King Louis II, with some 25,000 to 30,000 men at Mohács; the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent and the grand vizier Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha, perhaps 50,000, though some contemporary and modern historians put the number at 100,000
f.outcome: The Hungarian army was encircled and its lines collapsed within two hours; King Louis II drowned in flight. The Ottomans took Buda, then withdrew.
